notes: DECISIONS TAB REWORKED — assumptions, questions, and the arithmetic behind them now live on one screen. WHY: a decision is never judged in isolation. Buying a car in April 2027 depends on a child arriving, a parental-support commitment starting, a house loan later. Keeping those assumptions on a separate Scenarios page broke the only loop that matters: flip an assumption, watch the answer move. (1) ASSUMPTIONS IN PLAY sits at the top of the Decisions page with a live toggle per scenario; toggling re-evaluates every decision immediately. Scenarios can be added and edited from here through the existing editor, so the Scenarios page is never needed mid-analysis. That page is left untouched for anyone who prefers it. (2) MEASURE WHAT EACH ONE COSTS switches each assumption off in turn and reports the delay it causes in months, answering 'which of these is holding me back' directly. (3) THE FOUR TESTS ARE NOW EXPANDABLE, each showing its full working rather than a bare verdict. EMI vs income shows take-home split by earner, the percentage ceiling, the EMI, and the resulting headroom. Emergency cover shows the monthly running cost broken into household bills, existing EMIs, the contribution from your assumptions and this decision's own EMI; then the cover required; then liquid money split into cash and investments marked liquid. Every figure that produces the verdict is visible. Where no investment is flagged liquid the panel says so and points at Instruments, since that one flag can move the answer by months. (4) SIDE BY SIDE compares every decision in a single table — cost, EMI, month asked for, whether it works then, and the earliest month that does. Appears once there are two or more. (5) No charts on the page, by design. VERIFIED against real user data: with a Car Purchase assumption enabled, a Rs 14.42L car reads 'not in Apr 27'; toggling that assumption off moves it to 'yes from Nov 27'. Emergency cover at its tightest month reports running cost Rs 2,36,693 = household Rs 1,22,490 + existing EMIs Rs 52,000 + assumptions Rs 42,648 + this EMI Rs 19,554; cover needed Rs 14,20,159 against Rs 2,26,909 liquid; short by Rs 11,93,250. Side-by-side correctly separates Punch EV (2028-05) from Nexon EV (2028-06). Affordability remains monotonic across appetites (Rs 25.0L / 32.0L / 35.75L). Rapid switching between decisions leaves no stale panel. All other pages re-run clean. NOTE ON DOUBLE-COUNTING: an enabled purchase scenario is part of the world a decision is judged in, so an enabled 'Car Purchase' assumption means a car decision is tested as though a car had already been bought — two deposits, two EMIs. The toggles make that visible and reversible in one click, which is the reason for merging the two views. UNCHANGED: the projection engine, runProjection, the v2026.05.05.15 live-anchored EOM savings fix, and the one-off contamination and liquidity-definition corrections from v2026.05.06.02. A wrapper on renderScenarios keeps this page in step when a scenario is saved from the shared editor; the section render map still holds the original function, so there is no recursion.
